messages:
ashley: incident-bot flagged surge of 5xx (mainly 502/504) hitting inference-gateway-private-usw2. Customers on Private/VPC flows are reporting timeouts. dashboard: 12% error rate over baseline.
incident-bot: @oncall please investigate — error spike on route /v1/generate -> inference-gateway-private-usw2. Paging: oncall-tim, eng-sre-lina, netops-sanjay.
oncall-tim: seeing it in the SLO alerts. curl to gateway shows repeated 502 with HTML from upstream. quick check: traffic to inference backend is healthy from hosted pool. Suspect egress/NAT issue for private nodes. Starting packet checks.
netops-sanjay: on it. I ran a quick tcpdump on one affected private node (private-nat-03) — seeing a lot of retransmits to upstream model cluster and SNAT has many distinct ports in TIME_WAIT. Possible ephemeral port collision or SNAT exhaustion pattern.
eng-sre-lina: joining. Can you paste tcpdump snippet and iptables/nat table? Also need list of impacted customer route prefixes so we can correlate peering.
support-alex: customers reported: customer-a and customer-c have high tail latencies; customer-b seeing intermittent 502s on long prompt runs. I'm posting customer ticket IDs in case we need to notify.
netops-sanjay: tcpdump snippet:
```
14:32:21.123 IP 10.0.5.12.40328 > 10.1.2.50.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
14:32:21.223 IP 10.0.5.12.40328 > 10.1.2.50.443: Flags [R], seq 12346, win 0, length 0
```
lots of rapid SYN then RSTs. netstat -nat shows many sockets in TIME_WAIT and some in CLOSE_WAIT on nat instance.
eng-sre-lina: that points to asymmetric return path or gateway dropping ephemeral translations. Can we check the NAT instance logs and conntrack counters?
infra-miguel: conntrack dump shows many entries with short lifetimes and a spike in tcp states; also saw messages about conntrack table full on the node. `conntrack -S` shows 96% usage.
oncall-tim: if conntrack is filling, new flows may get dropped -> 502 from gateway because backend can't complete TCP handshake. Mitigation: we can increase conntrack max and also rotate the NAT instance.
netops-sanjay: I'm increasing nf_conntrack_max by 50% on the affected NAT appliance now, will monitor. Running: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` (was 350000). Also applying `conntrack -L | wc -l` to confirm drop.
support-alex: customer-ops-bob — please put a brief status update to the affected customers: "We are investigating elevated 502/504 from private VPC gateways; engineering is working on NAT/egress translation capacity and we'll update in 30m." Keep it minimal.
customer-ops-bob: posting short note now. also asking for any workaround like forcing hosted routing (not possible for private) — customers asked if they should retry, we suggested short retries.
eng-sre-lina: while netops adjusts conntrack, I'm patching a temporary iptables rule to aggressively expire tracked connections for established-but-idle flows older than 30s to free table entries: `conntrack -E -p tcp --state ESTABLISHED --timeout 30` (will run carefully). This is a bit surgical but should relieve pressure until we rotate NAT.
qa-ryan: throwing in quick regression check — are we seeing any traffic pattern change from large-batch prompts causing long-lived idle connections? logs show many tokens streaming requests that remain idle between chunks.
oncall-tim: yes, streaming chat sessions keep long-open sockets with minimal packets -> contributes to conntrack pressure.
netops-sanjay: I also found asymmetry in peer route advertisements: one transit-peering session to partner-net had a missing route for return path (prefix 10.1.2.0/24) — some replies are being routed via an alternate transit appliance that doesn't have SNAT state. That explains RSTs.
eng-sre-lina: OK that's a big clue. Two parallel issues: conntrack table saturation on primary NAT + transit-peering route mismatch causing asymmetric flows. Prioritize peering route fix then NAT rotation.
infra-miguel: spinning up replacement NAT instance (private-nat-04) in same AZ and beginning traffic drain. Will attach EIP and failover routes in 60s. prep: `ip route` changes + update HA proxy weights.
oncall-tim: Do the failover. Also enable additional logging on the gateway to capture 502 stack traces so we can differentiate between TCP-level failures and application-level downstream 502s.
incident-bot: NOTE: severity elevated to P1 (multiple paying Private customers impacted). Escalation: Eng leadership looped in if not resolved in 1 hour.
eng-sre-lina: while infra migrates NAT, I'm prepping a fallback policy to route affected customers to hosted inference cluster (non-private) as a last resort if errors continue >20m. This requires network approval and customer consent — prepped message template.
support-alex: please keep me posted; I'll update customer tickets every 15m.
netops-sanjay: peering fix applied: redistributed route for 10.1.2.0/24 to transit-peer, verifying with `traceroute` now shows symmetric path. conntrack pressure dropping from 96% -> 60% after NAT rotation started.
infra-miguel: NAT swap complete. new NAT instance shows healthy conntrack headroom. HA weights adjusted. Observability shows successful SYN/SYN-ACK handshakes resumed.
qa-ryan: running synthetic tests: 50 long-stream requests -> 0/50 502s now. baseline latency normal.
oncall-tim: alerting noise decreasing. error rate down to 1.4% (near baseline). Great work. Keep monitoring for 30m.
eng-sre-lina: postmortem notes to capture: 1) conntrack max tuned too low for streaming workloads (need workload-aware defaults). 2) peering route advertising bug in transit config allowed asymmetric return path during failover. 3) add rate-based conntrack eviction and improved observability to detect conntrack pressure earlier.
netops-sanjay: followups: implement healthcheck to detect missing route advertisements (BGP monitoring) and automated route reconciliation for transit peers.
customer-ops-bob: customers notified of mitigation; some asked for RCA and timeline. I'll coordinate with product for communications.
support-alex: I'm closing immediate customer tickets with note: "We mitigated root cause (peering route + NAT conntrack) and traffic was restored. RCA pending." Will attach timeline when available.
oncall-tim: handing off to eng-sre-lina for post-incident actions and to netops-sanjay for peering follow-ups. My shift ends in 20m — if anything regresses, please escalate to oncall-night.
eng-sre-lina: taking ownership for postmortem and followups. I'll start a brief doc and assign owners for the three action items. Thanks everyone.
incident-bot: Incident marked as mitigated at 14:47 UTC. Postmortem owner: eng-sre-lina. Severity: P1 -> Mitigated. Please confirm if anyone needs the handoff alert to remain open.
ashley: thanks team. quick retrospective note — consider adding a probe that opens many short-lived connections simulating streaming chunk gaps to surface conntrack stress in staging.
support-alex: noted. closing the live channel for now; will reopen if errors resurface.
customer-ops-bob: will follow up with customers tomorrow with estimated RCA ETA 48 hours.
eng-sre-lina: creating postmortem doc and will paste link here once ready. closing thread for live mitigation.
